<reason>B won by narrowing the live clash to what a default does to students a school can actually reach. After both sides treated enforcement as honor-code territory, B’s comparison was cleaner: a ban still asks the conscientious to compose, while permissible-by-default asks them to annotate a generated draft. A’s honesty/detector case was sharp, but it never neutralized that ordinary obedient case, and reading “process transparency” as a required fail of disclosed outsourcing stretched the motion. A also paid a small execution cost for a clipped opening.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B’s first rebuttal recast A’s fabrication symmetry: if determined cheaters cheat under either rule, policy is decided by the instruction the conscientious follow. A never recovered a blank-page requirement from the motion.</best_rebuttal>
